overview: White plays 1.f3 e5 2.Kf2, moving the king to f2 on move two, a joke or surprise choice. Black simply develops with ...Nc6 and ...d5, or can harass the king with ...Qh4+ ideas, taking the centre while White lags in development. It is played for novelty and humour, not for objective merit.

white_ideas.idea: Accept a loss of castling and hope Black overreaches
Follow with e4, d4 or Nc3 and bring the king to safety later

black_ideas.idea: Attack the king with ...Qh4+ and ...Bc5+ when possible

typical_structures.structure: Black holds e5 and the centre while White king sits on f2, f3 pawn blocks the knight

character.notes: Early king move and an unfinished set-up give unbalanced, risky play, mostly for White.

gambit.notes: No material is given up on purpose.

soundness.notes: Worse for White since the king loses castling and f3 blocks the knight.

structure.notes: The centre depends on whether Black plays ...d5 and White follows with e4; unclear.

approach.notes: Almost never seen outside blitz and humour.

level.notes: A dubious line, not a good repertoire choice.

character.reason: The early king move leads to unbalanced play with tactical risk.

gambit.reason: No pawn is sacrificed on purpose.

soundness.reason: King on f2 and f3 lose time and castling.

structure.reason: Black takes the centre and the lines open after ...d5 and e4.
